transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, they... my family brought me in. They say I’m here because I went and used up our savings on wood, lights, and all this display stuff for the yard. I kept pushing the work, you know, staying up way after dark, hammering and wiring out there. But I felt like if I stopped, the whole house—hell, the whole block—would lose its chance. It was important. 

Speaking of the block, the fella down at the end of the street, Frank, he used to have this beautiful oak tree in his front yard. Cut it down back in, oh, must've been '98. I told him, I said, "Frank, you’re gonna miss that shade," and sure enough, his lawn just burned right up the very next July. Dead grass everywhere. I used to do a lot of yard work before my knees went bad. You can’t just plant anything in this soil around here, it’s got way too much clay in it. I was trying to explain that to the kid at the hardware store when I was buying the extension cords for the display, but he didn’t know a thing about dirt. Just wanted to scan my card and look at his phone. Kids these days don't know the value of a good day's work outdoors anyway... what were we talking about?
Did you feel like your yard display was going to be the best on the block or even in the whole town?

Well, best on the block? Oh, it was going to be more than that. I honestly believe I can turn that old Schiller Park house into something important, you know? Something people will travel from all over just to come see. Because nobody understands light and pictures the way I do. I see the angles, the way the glow hits the siding. It’s like a gift. 

Speaking of gifts, my grandson, he got this drone thing for Christmas last year. Little plastic thing with four propellers. Buzzes like a hornet. He was flying it all over the living room, knocking down my wife's porcelain angels. She collects those, you know. Started collecting them back in '85 when we took that trip down to Florida. We drove the whole way in that old station wagon. The AC went out somewhere around Georgia, and let me tell you, it was hotter than a furnace in there. We had to roll the windows down, but the noise on the highway was just terrible. I haven't been back to Florida since... too humid. What was the question again?
Did you feel unusually energetic or restless while working on your yard display?

Energetic? Well, sure, I suppose. I just can’t sit in my chair anymore. I’m up moving constantly, going from the garden to the darkroom to the porch, carrying tools around and fixing things before anyone even asks me to. Just gotta keep at it. 

You know, speaking of that chair, it’s a real nice corduroy recliner we bought at Sears years ago. You remember when they had a Sears over at the Eastland Mall? It’s a crying shame what happened to that mall. All boarded up now, just a big empty parking lot full of weeds. I took my daughter there to get her ears pierced when she was... oh, must have been twelve. She cried the whole way home. We had to stop and get her a vanilla cone at the Dairy Queen just to quiet her down. Ice cream used to taste better back then, didn't it? Real milk. Now it's all chemicals and high fructose whatever they call it. I read an article about that in the Sunday paper. I still get the physical paper delivered, I can't stand reading the news on a screen, hurts my eyes. The delivery boy throws it right in the hydrangeas half the time though. I've told him twice to aim for the driveway... wait, what were we talking about? Did you ask about the porch?
Have you been feeling unusually happy or excited lately?

Happy? Oh, most days I feel completely charged up, yeah. Almost joyful, really, like I’m a young man again! I’ve got all this life in me. But then, you know, if my wife or those contractors I brought in start questioning me or telling me how to do things, I get hot real fast. I just lose it and start yelling at them. 

I mean, I hired these guys to lay some extra concrete for the yard displays, and they think they know better than me. The price of concrete is ridiculous these days anyway. Back when I was doing day labor in the 70s—I went straight to work, didn't bother finishing high school, didn't need to—we used to mix it all by hand. Me and my buddy Ray, we'd be out there sweating buckets. Ray had this old Chevy truck, baby blue. Beautiful machine, but the transmission slipped in second gear. We drove that thing all the way up to Chicago once just to see a ballgame. Wrigley Field. The hot dogs there, they put celery salt on them, can you believe that? I never understood celery salt. It just tastes like dust to me. My wife loves it, though. Puts it in her potato salad every Fourth of July. She makes a massive bowl of it, but she always uses way too much mayonnaise. It gets all soupy if it sits out in the sun for more than ten minutes. I keep telling her to keep it in the cooler, but she never listens... wait, what were you asking me? Did you want to know about the contractors?
Have you had periods in your life where you felt extremely low or depressed?

Low? Depressed? No, no, I don't think so. I don't really get down like that. I've always been a pretty steady guy, mostly. Well, except for right now with all this energy, but no, not depressed. 

You know, speaking of feeling low, my buddy Ray—the one with the Chevy I was telling you about—he used to get real low back in the day. He had this old hound dog, Buster, that passed away, and Ray just wasn't the same for months. Buster was a good dog, though. Used to howl at the mailman every single day at exactly 11:30. You could set your watch by it. The mailman's name was Gary, wore those little blue shorts even in November. I never understood how guys could wear shorts when it's freezing out. My knees ache just thinking about it. I've had bad knees since I fell off a ladder cleaning the gutters back in '98. The wife told me to hire someone, but I said, "Why pay a guy when I can do it myself?" Ended up costing me more in hospital bills anyway. They put me in this cast that went all the way up my thigh, and it itched like crazy. I had to use a wire coat hanger just to scratch my leg. Do they even make wire coat hangers anymore? Everything is plastic now. Plastic breaks too easy... wait, what were you asking me? Did you want to know about my knees?
Have you ever had a period where you felt as energetic and happy as you do now for an extended time before?

Before? No, I don't think I've ever felt quite like this before. It's been going on for about three months now, ever since the remodeling started and everything in the house got turned upside down. 

It’s been a real mess, let me tell you. Dust everywhere. You can't even walk into the kitchen without getting drywall dust on your slippers. I bought a new pair of those sheepskin ones from L.L. Bean just before Christmas, and they’re already ruined. Christmas was a quiet one this year, though. My daughter usually comes down from Michigan, but the weather was so bad she couldn't make the drive. The snow up there gets up to your waist, I swear. I remember one winter, back in '78, we had a blizzard so bad the plows didn't come down our street for three days. We lived on Elm Street back then, right next to the Johnsons. Good people, the Johnsons. Mr. Johnson had this incredible collection of model trains in his basement. He’d spend hours down there painting those tiny little trees and laying tracks. I never had the patience for it. My hands shake too much for that kind of detail work. Probably from all the coffee I drink. I need at least three cups just to get my engine running in the morning. Black, no sugar. Sugar rots your teeth out, that's what my old dentist used to say. Dr. Miller. He had breath that smelled like peppermint and stale cigars... wait, what were we talking about? Did you ask about the kitchen remodeling?
Have you ever had a time when you felt extremely low after a period of feeling as energetic and happy as you do now?

Low after feeling like this? No, I told you, I don't really get low. I've never felt this charged up before anyway, so there's nothing to come down from. 

Speaking of coming down, though, you should see the way the oak tree in my front yard is coming down. Branches everywhere. The city said they were going to trim it back in October, but did they? Of course not. You can't rely on the city for anything these days. It's like the garbage collection. They switched to those automated trucks with the mechanical arms, and half the time they knock the bins over and just leave the trash in the street. I had to go out there with a broom in my bathrobe last Tuesday. It was a green bathrobe, terrycloth. My wife got it for me at a Macy's sale. Macy's isn't what it used to be, you know. Used to be you could go in there and get real service. The shoe salesman would actually measure your foot with one of those metal sliding things. What are those called? A Brannock device, I think. My uncle Arthur sold shoes for thirty years down in St. Louis. He always said a man is only as good as his footwear. He wore these beautiful leather wingtips, polished them every Sunday night while listening to the radio. Mostly big band stuff. Glenn Miller, Tommy Dorsey. They don't make music like that anymore, just noise now. All thump-thump-thump from the cars driving by... wait, what was the question? Did you want to know about my uncle Arthur?
Have you ever had a time when you felt extremely energetic and happy like you do now, and then later felt extremely low?

Like I said, Doc, no. I don't get low, and I've never been this wired up before, so I haven't had a chance to go from one to the other. 

But you know, talking about going from one extreme to the other, the weather around here has been doing exactly that. One day it's sixty degrees and sunny, the next day there's frost on the windshield. It plays absolute havoc with my tomatoes. I've got three Big Boy plants out back, and I've had to cover them with old bedsheets twice this week just to keep them from freezing. My wife hates when I use the good sheets, but what am I supposed to do? Let the tomatoes die? I take pride in my garden. My grandfather was a farmer, you know. Grew corn and soybeans down in Illinois. He used to wake up at four in the morning every single day, even on Sundays. Said the Lord's day was no excuse for laziness. He had this old John Deere tractor, green and yellow, sounded like a washing machine full of rocks when it started up. He let me drive it once when I was twelve. I nearly took out a fence post, but he just laughed. He had a great laugh, my grandfather. Sounded like a booming drum. He smoked a pipe, too. Cherry tobacco. The smell of it always reminds me of... wait, what were you asking me about? The weather?
Have you ever felt extremely low after a period of feeling extremely energetic and happy?

Are you... are you asking me the same thing again? I feel like we just went over this. No, I haven't. I haven't felt low, and I haven't been this energetic before, so there's no "after." 

Speaking of after, though, the contractor said he'd be here after lunch to fix the drywall, but he never showed. Never showed! You just can't get good help anymore. It's like that time I tried to hire a kid from the neighborhood to mow the lawn. Billy, I think his name was. Or maybe Tommy. He had red hair, lots of freckles. Anyway, he charged me twenty bucks, went over my wife's prize petunias with the mower, and then left the clippings all over the driveway. I had to sweep them up myself. I used that push broom we keep in the garage, the one with the stiff bristles. I bought it at the hardware store downtown before it closed. Miller's Hardware, it was called. Old Mr. Miller ran the place for fifty years. He always had a jar of butterscotch candies on the counter. The kind wrapped in that yellow cellophane. I haven't had a butterscotch candy in years. They get stuck in my teeth now. My dentist says I need a crown on my back molar, but I don't want to go in. The drill sound gives me the creeps. Sounds like a mosquito buzzing right in your ear. I hate mosquitoes. Summer evenings used to be ruined by them until they started spraying the neighborhood. The truck would come by blowing this thick white fog... wait, why are you asking me the same question three times? Did you want to know about the contractor?
Have you ever had a period of feeling extremely energetic and happy like this before in your life?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I've had good days, sure, but not... not like this. I feel like I could run a marathon right now, and I haven't run anywhere since 1978. 

That was the year we went to Florida, actually. Drove the whole way down in a station wagon. Wood paneling on the sides, you know the kind? It got so hot in that car, the vinyl seats would stick to the back of your legs. My wife packed egg salad sandwiches in a cooler, but the ice melted by the time we hit Georgia, and let me tell you, warm egg salad is a mistake you only make once. We stopped at this diner off the highway to use the restroom, and they had a jukebox in the corner. Plays three songs for a quarter. I put in a quarter and played Johnny Cash. "Ring of Fire," I think it was. Great song. They don't have jukeboxes in diners anymore. Now it's all just some satellite radio station playing softly in the ceiling. You can barely hear it over the clattering of the plates. I hate a noisy restaurant. We went to this Italian place last week for our anniversary, and the waiter kept dropping the silverware. Clang, clang, clang on the tile floor. I almost told him to just leave it there. He brought out the garlic bread, though, and it was fantastic. Real butter, not that margarine stuff. Margarine is basically plastic anyway, did you know that? I read an article about it in a magazine at the barber shop. The barber, Sal, he's been cutting my hair for twenty years. He's got this old leather chair that squeaks every time he pumps the pedal. He uses a straight razor on the back of the neck, hot lather and everything... wait, what were you asking me? About the marathon?
Have you ever experienced a significant drop in mood or energy after a period of feeling extremely happy or energetic?

Doc, are you pulling my leg here? I feel like we're stuck on a merry-go-round. No, I haven't had a drop in my mood after feeling like this, because I've never felt like this before in my entire life! And I certainly don't feel low right now. 

Speaking of merry-go-rounds, though, they took the old one out of the park down the street. It was one of those heavy metal ones, you know? Painted red and blue. Kids used to spin that thing so fast somebody would always end up flying off into the dirt. It was dangerous, sure, but that was half the fun. Now they replaced it with this... this plastic contraption. Looks like a giant colorful mushroom. It doesn't even spin fast. Everything's too safe nowadays. Like those rubber mats they put under the swings instead of woodchips. When I was a kid, if you fell off the swing, you got a scrape on your knee and you learned to hold on tighter next time. We used to put Mercurochrome on cuts. Stung like the dickens and dyed your skin orange for a week. My mother had a little glass bottle of it in the medicine cabinet. That medicine cabinet had a mirror that was starting to peel away at the edges, getting all cloudy. She kept her cold cream in there, too. Ponds, I think it was. Smelled like roses and powder. She'd put it on every night before bed, said it kept the wrinkles away. She lived to be eighty-nine, so maybe she was onto something. She made the best pot roast, too. Cooked it slow all Sunday afternoon with carrots and those little pearl onions. I can almost smell it right now... wait, what did you ask me? Did you want the pot roast recipe?
Have you ever had periods in your life where you felt extremely energetic and happy, followed by periods where you felt extremely low, in a repeating pattern?

Are you... are you messing with me, Doc? Is this a test? We've been over this, haven't we? I swear you just asked me this. No! No repeating pattern, no up and down, no nothing. I've never felt this good, this wired, ever. So there's no pattern to it. 

Patterns, though... you know, my wife used to make her own dresses using those paper patterns. McCall's, I think the brand was. Or maybe Simplicity. They came in these flimsy little envelopes, and the paper was so thin, like tissue paper. You'd lay it out on the dining room table and pin it to the fabric. She made this one dress for my niece's wedding back in '85. It was a lovely shade of peach. Peach was very popular in the eighties. Everything was peach and seafoam green. Even our bathroom tile was seafoam green. We had to scrub the grout with an old toothbrush to keep the mildew away. I used an old Colgate toothbrush, the kind with the hard bristles. Dentists say you're supposed to use soft bristles now so you don't wear away the enamel. Enamel's important, you know. Once it's gone, it's gone. Like the topsoil in the Dust Bowl. I read a book about the Dust Bowl once. Fascinating stuff. The dirt just blew away because they plowed up all the deep-rooted prairie grass. You have to have strong roots. My grandfather was a farmer, actually. Grew corn and soybeans out in Ohio. He had a tractor, an old John Deere. Painted that classic green and yellow. He'd let me steer it sometimes when I was a boy, sitting right on his lap... wait, why do you keep asking me the same thing? Did you want to know about my grandfather's farm?
Have you ever had a period in your life where you felt as energetic and happy as you do now, before these past three months?

Doc, I feel like a broken record here, I really do. Are your ears working alright? No, never before this! It's just been these past three months. This whole thing just started about three months ago, right when the remodeling started and everything in the house got turned completely upside down. 

You wouldn't believe the mess. Dust on every single surface. The contractor, his name is Bill, or maybe Bob... anyway, he drives this massive pickup truck that takes up my entire driveway. It's a Ford. Cherry red. My brother Tommy used to have a Ford, actually. A '69 Mustang. Now that was a beautiful piece of machinery. We used to take it down to the drive-in theater on Route 9 on Friday nights. You'd pull up and hook that heavy little metal speaker right onto the window glass. The sound was always a little crackly, but you didn't care. We saw that Clint Eastwood picture there, The Good, the Bad, and the Ugly. Fantastic movie. They don't make westerns like that anymore. Now you go to the pictures and it's just a bunch of people in tight spandex suits flying around shooting lasers out of their hands. My grandson, he loves that superhero junk. He leaves those little plastic action figures all over his bedroom floor. Let me tell you, if you get up to use the john in the middle of the night and step on one of those pointy plastic capes in your bare feet, you will know what true pain is. It's worse than stepping on a rusty nail. I stepped on a nail once when I was building a treehouse out back in the big oak tree. Went right through the sole of my work boot. Had to go get a tetanus shot from old Dr. Higgins. He had a glass jar of lollipops on his desk, even for the adults... wait, what were you asking me? Did you want to know about the treehouse?
Have you ever had another period in your life where you felt as energetic and happy as you do now, before these past three months?

Doc, are you deaf or just trying to drive me crazy? I just told you! No! Never! Never in my whole seventy-three years have I felt this fantastic before three months ago. I feel like I'm talking to a brick wall here. 

Speaking of brick walls, my neighbor, Frank, he built this beautiful brick retaining wall in his backyard. Did it all by himself, mixing the mortar in a wheelbarrow. He used those red clay bricks, you know the ones with the holes in the middle? He said it helps the mortar grip better. Frank's a smart guy, used to work for the post office. He knows everyone's business because he delivered the mail for thirty years. He told me once that the amount of junk mail people get is astronomical. Catalogs for things you'd never buy in a million years. Like, who needs a catalog just for specialty birdhouses? I mean, I like birds, don't get me wrong. We used to have a bird feeder out by the kitchen window. The cardinals would come every morning. Bright red, beautiful birds. My wife loved them. She used to buy this special seed mix with extra black oil sunflower seeds. The squirrels figured out how to get into it, though. Clever little devils. They'd shimmy down the wire and hang upside down just to steal the seeds. I tried putting grease on the pole, but they just slid down and landed in the bushes. Bushes... we had azaleas. Bright pink ones. They only bloom for a couple of weeks in the spring, but when they do, it's quite a show. You have to make sure the soil is acidic enough, though, or the leaves turn yellow. I used to put pine needles around the base to keep the acid up... wait, what did you ask me? Did you want to know how to keep squirrels out of your bird feeder?
Have you ever had a period in your life where you felt extremely energetic and happy, and then it went away, only to come back again?

Doc, I... I don't know what kind of game you're playing here. Are you trying to trick me? I've answered this! I told you, no. It didn't happen, then go away, then come back. It's just now. Just these last three months, straight through. Never before. 

It's like... it's like you're a skipping record, Doc. You know, we used to have a record player, a real nice one in a wooden console. Solid mahogany. We had it in the living room, right next to the sofa. The sofa had this horrible floral print, but it was comfortable. My mother picked it out. She had terrible taste in furniture, bless her heart. She loved anything with big, loud flowers on it. She even had floral wallpaper in the kitchen. Yellow and orange daisies. It was blinding in the morning when the sun hit it. We lived in this house on Elm Street, had a big bay window in the front. You could see the whole neighborhood from there. Mrs. Gable across the street, she was always out sweeping her porch. Every single day, sweeping, sweeping. I don't know where all the dirt came from. She had this old straw broom, the kind that sheds pieces everywhere. You'd think she was making more of a mess than she was cleaning up. I bought one of those plastic brooms once, the ones with the angled bristles? Supposed to get into the corners better. But it just pushed the dust around. Didn't pick up a darn thing. You really need a good vacuum cleaner for that. We had a Hoover. Heavy as a tank, but it could suck the chrome off a bumper. The bag was always a pain to change, though. You'd pull it out and a big cloud of dust would puff up in your face, make you sneeze... wait, what are we talking about? Did you need me to fix your vacuum cleaner?
Have you ever felt this energetic and happy before, and if so, did it stop and then come back?

Doc, are you pulling my leg? Is this... am I on Candid Camera or something? I swear, you're asking me the exact same thing again. No! Never! Just the last three months, straight as an arrow. Never before, it didn't come and go, nothing. 

I feel like there's a camera hidden in that potted plant over there. We used to watch Candid Camera all the time. Allen Funt, right? That was a funny show. We had this old Zenith television set, the kind that took up half the living room. Heavy wood cabinet. You had to let it warm up for five minutes before the picture would even think about coming in, and even then, half the time it was just snow. My dad used to make me stand by the set and hold the rabbit ears so we could watch the baseball game. If I moved an inch, the picture would roll. We tried wrapping aluminum foil on the tips of the antennas. Supposed to boost the signal, you know? My mother used a lot of aluminum foil. She'd wrap baked potatoes in it before she put them in the oven. Left them in there for hours until the skin was practically leather. She made the best mashed potatoes, though. Used real butter and heavy cream. None of that margarine garbage. Margarine is just oil and yellow food coloring, you know. I read an article in the Reader's Digest about how they make it in these big vats. Sounds like a chemical plant. My uncle worked at a chemical plant down in Delaware. Smelled like sulfur all the time. He used to bring home these little plastic hard hats for me and Tommy... wait, what did you ask me? Did you want to know about my uncle's hats?
Have you ever had a period in your life where you felt extremely energetic and happy, and then later felt extremely low, and then felt extremely energetic and happy again?

Doc, what is wrong with you? Seriously, are you okay? I feel like I'm stuck in some kind of loop here! I've told you, over and over and over again. No! I have never felt this good, and I have never felt low, and it never went away and came back. This is it. Just these last three months. Period. 

You know, talking to you is like trying to get my old Ford to start on a cold morning. You just keep grinding the starter and nothing happens. Grrr, grrr, grrr. I had this '68 Ford F-150. Beautiful truck. Two-tone, blue and white. It had a three-on-the-tree manual transmission. You don't see those anymore. Kids today wouldn't know how to drive one if their lives depended on it. Everything's automatic now. Push a button, the car parks itself. Where's the skill in that? I used to change my own oil, spark plugs, the whole nine yards. Getting under the hood, getting your hands dirty... that's how you really know a machine. I had this grease monkey friend, Sal. Sal owned a garage down on 4th Street. Place smelled like gasoline and old coffee. He had this calendar on the wall, one of those Snap-on Tools calendars with the girls in the swimsuits... you know the ones? My wife hated that calendar. She wouldn't even step foot in the garage. She said it was disrespectful. But Sal was a good guy. He gave me a discount on tires once when things were tight. Tires are so expensive now. Steel-belted radials, all-season... back then, you just got a tire and hoped it didn't blow out on the highway. I had a blowout once on Interstate 95. Scariest thing in my life. The truck swerved across three lanes of traffic. Thank God it was late at night and no one else was around. Just me and the moonlight... wait, what were we just saying? Did you want to know about my tires?
Do you think you might feel extremely low or depressed after this period of feeling extremely energetic and happy is over?

Why would I feel low? I feel like a million bucks right now, Doc! I mean, this energy, it's incredible. I don't see any reason why it would just stop and drop me down into some kind of hole. I'm on top of the world! 

It's like when we finally got to the top of the Empire State Building. Have you ever been up there? The observation deck? The wind just whips right through you, but the view... you can see all the way to New Jersey on a clear day. We went up there in '76, for the Bicentennial. The whole city was painted red, white, and blue. They had tall ships in the harbor, fireworks going off over the Statue of Liberty. It was a madhouse, people everywhere, shoulder to shoulder. My youngest, he was just a little tyke then, he lost his balloon. Let go of the string and it just sailed right up into the sky. He cried for an hour, wouldn't let it go. We tried buying him ice cream, hot dogs, nothing worked. Kids get so attached to the silliest things. I remember I had this little wooden top when I was a boy. You'd wrap a string around it and throw it, and it would spin for ages. My brother stepped on it and cracked it right down the middle. I was so mad, I wouldn't speak to him for a week. We shared a room, too, so it was a lot of angry staring across the space between the twin beds. We had these scratchy wool blankets, army surplus. Kept you warm in the winter, but they itched like crazy. You had to wear long johns just to sleep. Long johns with the little trap door in the back... wait, what did you ask me? Did you want to know about my brother?
Do you think it's possible that after this period of feeling extremely energetic and happy is over, you might feel extremely low or depressed?

Doc, are we... is there an echo in here? I swear you just asked me that! I just told you, I'm on top of the world! Why would I crash? I feel fantastic, I don't see any reason I'd suddenly feel low. 

It's like asking if the sun's gonna suddenly fall out of the sky. The sun just keeps shining, right? Well, except when there's an eclipse. We saw a partial eclipse back in... oh, must have been the late nineties. The local library was handing out those little cardboard glasses so you wouldn't burn your retinas out. You know, you look at the sun and you can go blind. My grandfather went blind, but that was from glaucoma, not the sun. He had these thick, thick glasses, like looking through the bottom of a Coca-Cola bottle. Real glass, too, heavy on the nose. He used to sit in his armchair all day listening to the radio. AM radio, talk shows, baseball games. He loved the Mets. I never cared for the Mets, I was a Yankees man myself. The Bronx Bombers! Mickey Mantle, Joe DiMaggio... now those were ballplayers. DiMaggio had that streak, 56 games. Nobody's ever gonna touch that. They don't make them like they used to. Now they get paid millions of dollars just to strike out. It's a crying shame. We used to play stickball in the street until the streetlights came on. We'd use a broom handle and a pink Spaldeen ball. If you hit it over the telephone wires, it was an automatic home run. You had to watch out for Mrs. Gable's window, though. She was a mean old bird, always threatening to call the cops if we made too much noise. She had this tiny little dog, a Chihuahua, I think. Ugliest thing you ever saw, looked like a rat that got stuck in a toaster. Yapped all day long. Yap, yap, yap... kinda like... wait, what were you asking me? Did you want to know about Mrs. Gable's dog?

doctor.question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

target_item.name: Painful_Consequence_Behavior
target_item.manifestation: They say I’m here because I used our savings on wood, lights, and display stuff and kept pushing the work after dark, but I felt like if I stopped, the whole house and block would lose its chance.
target_item.reason: This is the first reply of the consultation, so I must return the chief complaint symptom code (S041) regardless of the doctor's opening question.

patient.answer:
Well, they... my family brought me in. They say I’m here because I went and used up our savings on wood, lights, and all this display stuff for the yard. I kept pushing the work, you know, staying up way after dark, hammering and wiring out there. But I felt like if I stopped, the whole house—hell, the whole block—would lose its chance. It was important.

Why would I feel low? I feel like a million bucks right now, Doc! I mean, this energy, it's incredible. I don't see any reason why it would just stop and drop me down into some kind of hole. I'm on top of the world! 

It's like when we finally got to the top of the Empire State Building. Have you ever been up there? The observation deck? The wind just whips right through you, but the view... you can see all the way to New Jersey on a clear day. We went up there in '76, for the Bicentennial. The whole city was painted red, white, and blue. They had tall ships in the harbor, fireworks going off over the Statue of Liberty. It was a madhouse, people everywhere, shoulder to shoulder. My youngest, he was just a little tyke then, he lost his balloon. Let go of the string and it just sailed right up into the sky. He cried for an hour, wouldn't let it go. We tried buying him ice cream, hot dogs, nothing worked. Kids get so attached to the silliest things. I remember I had this little wooden top when I was a boy. You'd wrap a string around it and throw it, and it would spin for ages. My brother stepped on it and cracked it right down the middle. I was so mad, I wouldn't speak to him for a week. We shared a room, too, so it was a lot of angry staring across the space between the twin beds. We had these scratchy wool blankets, army surplus. Kept you warm in the winter, but they itched like crazy. You had to wear long johns just to sleep. Long johns with the little trap door in the back... wait, what did you ask me? Did you want to know about my brother?

doctor.question: Do you think it's possible that after this period of feeling extremely energetic and happy is over, you might feel extremely low or depressed?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the possibility of a future depressive episode (feeling extremely low or depressed), which is not covered by any of the symptoms in my profile.

patient.answer:
Doc, are we... is there an echo in here? I swear you just asked me that! I just told you, I'm on top of the world! Why would I crash? I feel fantastic, I don't see any reason I'd suddenly feel low. 

It's like asking if the sun's gonna suddenly fall out of the sky. The sun just keeps shining, right? Well, except when there's an eclipse. We saw a partial eclipse back in... oh, must have been the late nineties. The local library was handing out those little cardboard glasses so you wouldn't burn your retinas out. You know, you look at the sun and you can go blind. My grandfather went blind, but that was from glaucoma, not the sun. He had these thick, thick glasses, like looking through the bottom of a Coca-Cola bottle. Real glass, too, heavy on the nose. He used to sit in his armchair all day listening to the radio. AM radio, talk shows, baseball games. He loved the Mets. I never cared for the Mets, I was a Yankees man myself. The Bronx Bombers! Mickey Mantle, Joe DiMaggio... now those were ballplayers. DiMaggio had that streak, 56 games. Nobody's ever gonna touch that. They don't make them like they used to. Now they get paid millions of dollars just to strike out. It's a crying shame. We used to play stickball in the street until the streetlights came on. We'd use a broom handle and a pink Spaldeen ball. If you hit it over the telephone wires, it was an automatic home run. You had to watch out for Mrs. Gable's window, though. She was a mean old bird, always threatening to call the cops if we made too much noise. She had this tiny little dog, a Chihuahua, I think. Ugliest thing you ever saw, looked like a rat that got stuck in a toaster. Yapped all day long. Yap, yap, yap... kinda like... wait, what were you asking me? Did you want to know about Mrs. Gable's dog?
